### According to Flora Zambesiaca under the synonym Plectranthus hadiensis

J. R. Timberlake, E. S. Martins (2013). Flora Zambesiaca, Vol 8: part 8. Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew

Type
    Type: Yemen, Hadiyah (Hadi) Mts, Forsskål s.n. (C holotype).
Morphology General Habit
    Perennial herb 0.2–1.5 m tall, succulent or slightly so, occasionally with thickened roots; aromatic- Stems rounded-quadrangular, procumbent, scandent or weakly ascending, sometimes mat or clump-forming, branched, purplish above, older stem sometimes with conspicuous leaf scars, villose to pubescent with long spreading and retrorse eglandular and usually shorter glandular hairs, usually with scattered red sessile glands on inflorescence axis
Morphology Leaves
    Leaves spreading, petiolate, slightly succulent, sometimes with clusters of younger leaf in axils; blade 10–50(60– 120) × 10–50(60–110) mm, ovate to triangular, crenate or dentate with deltate teeth, weakly revolute, apex rounded or obtuse, base rarely cordate, truncate or broadly cuneate, pubescent to tomentose, with pale and sometimes red sessile glands beneath; petioles 7–50 mm long
Morphology Reproductive morphology Inflorescences
    Inflorescence lax with 4–12(20)-flowered verticils 10–20 mm apart, bract subtending opposite, sessile, 2–6(10)-flowered cymes; bract 1–3 mm long, erect above forming an inconspicuous terminal coma, soon deciduous below; pedicel (2)3–6(9) mm long, mostly spreading
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Calyx
    Calyx 1–2 mm long, pubescent with red sessile glands; fruiting calyx 3–6 mm long, tubular, slightly curved, pedicel attached eccentrically behind posterior lip; throat truncate; posterior lip elliptic, purple, shortly decurrent, slightly curved upwards; anterior lobes lanceolate with median lobes slightly narrower and longer than laterals
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Corolla
    Corolla blue or purple, 6–13 mm long, glabrous or pubescent, red sessile glands on lobes; tube (2)4–6 mm long, shallowly sigmoid, dorsally convex at bend; posterior lip shorter than anterior
Morphology Reproductive morphology Flowers Androecium Stamens Filaments
    Staminal filaments free
Morphology Reproductive morphology Fruits
    Nutlets brown shiny with reddish dots; 1 mm long, broadly elliptic, flattened; producing lots of mucilage speckled on outer surface.
Distribution
    Zimbabwe, Malawi, Mozambique. Egypt to South Africa, Arabian Peninsula, Sri Lanka.
Ecology
    Rocky soil or outcrops, rocky areas in Acacia–Commiphora scrub or deciduous woodland; 800–2100 m.
Conservation
    Widespread; Least Concern.
Recognition
    There seems to be a general pattern in tropical Africa (excluding South Africa) that material from S Tanzania and the Flora Zambesiaca region often has larger leaves with longer petioles. In East Africa, material from upland Kenya tends to have longer pedicels and larger mature calyces than material from Uganda and coastal areas, but there are no clear discontinuities.
